plans.rawRequirement: Invoice tax is wrong: CGST and SGST come out reversed on interstate orders. Fix it; the old invoices may need correcting too.
plans.businessRequirement: For an interstate sale the invoice must charge IGST against the place of supply. Today the system charges CGST+SGST against the billing state, so 41 invoices raised since 12 Aug carry the wrong tax heads and the wrong total.
plans.technicalRequirement: Resolve tax jurisdiction once, in TaxService.ResolveJurisdiction, from the place-of-supply on the sales order — not from MST_CUSTOMER.state_code. SP_CalculateTax must consume the resolved jurisdiction instead of re-deriving it from the billing address at L288. Existing rounding behaviour is a contract and must not move.
plans.architectureImpact: Introduces ITaxJurisdictionResolver as the single source of jurisdiction. SP_CalculateTax loses a derivation branch and gains a required parameter — a signature change on a procedure with 11 callers, so every caller is updated in the same worktree. TRANS_INVOICE is never written directly (MEM-142); the backfill goes through SP_CommitTaxCorrection.

memory.title: Architecture Decision #142 — TRANS table must not be directly modified
memory.body: No service, script or agent may INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE on any TRANS_* table directly. All writes go through SP_PostTransaction, which stamps the audit trio (POSTED_BY, POSTED_ON, POSTED_MACHINE) and writes the paired row into TRANS_LEDGER. Direct writes leave the ledger unbalanced and the month-end close silently reports a wrong figure.
memory.reason: Legacy accounting integration.

memory.title: Repository layer is the only place raw SQL is allowed
memory.body: Services take an I<Name>Repository via constructor injection. A service that opens a SqlConnection is an automatic review rejection. Reviewer agent greps for "new SqlConnection" outside src/Data/ on every diff.
memory.reason: Two 2023 incidents traced back to ad-hoc SQL inside services bypassing the retry policy.
memory.source: ADR-19 + Code Reviewer rejection pattern (14 occurrences)

memory.title: HIMS billing talks to ERP only over the PMI compatibility contract
memory.body: HIMS v3 never reads CAREWORKS tables directly. Everything crosses through the PMI contract views (VW_PMI_PATIENT, VW_PMI_CHARGE). The views are versioned; breaking one requires a dual-write window of at least one billing cycle.
memory.reason: Both systems are live at the same hospitals during the renewal.

memory.title: Frontend state: no new state library, ever
memory.body: React Context + useReducer for cross-screen state, local useState for everything else. TanStack Query only for server cache. A PR that adds Zustand/Redux/Jotai gets closed without review.
memory.reason: Four state libraries already died in this codebase between 2013 and 2021; the migration cost each time was measured in months.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2025-01-09 ("do not bring in a new state library; use the one we have")

memory.title: Interstate supply is CGST/SGST only when supplier state == place of supply
memory.body: If MST_CUSTOMER.STATE_CODE != MST_BRANCH.STATE_CODE the invoice is IGST at the full slab. Same-state is split CGST + SGST at half the slab each. The exception is SEZ customers (MST_CUSTOMER.SEZ_FLAG = 1) — always IGST, zero-rated, regardless of state.
memory.reason: Section 7/8 IGST Act; the SEZ carve-out has burned the team twice.
memory.source: CA sign-off note 2025-06-20 + BUG-883 root cause

memory.title: Tax rounding is per line item, then invoice total — never the reverse
memory.body: Each line rounds to 2 decimals with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, then lines sum to the invoice total. Rounding the total instead of the lines shifts ₹0.01–₹0.04 per invoice and the reconciliation job flags it.
memory.reason: The legacy VB6 module rounded this way and 11 years of posted invoices depend on it matching.

memory.title: Credit note cannot exceed the original invoice net of prior credit notes
memory.body: SP_CreateCreditNote checks SUM(CN.AMOUNT) + new amount <= TRANS_INVOICE.NET_AMOUNT. Over-credit is a hard failure, not a warning — finance treats it as fraud surface.
memory.reason: Statutory audit finding FY2023-24.

memory.title: IPD bill freezes at discharge; only the pharmacy return window stays open 24 h
memory.body: After DISCHARGE_STATUS = 2, charges are read-only except PHARM_RETURN lines posted within 24 hours. Anything later needs a supervisor override with a reason code, stored in TRANS_OVERRIDE.
memory.reason: Insurance TPAs reject bills whose totals change after the discharge summary is issued.

memory.title: MST_TAX is slab-versioned by effective date, not overwritten
memory.body: Rate changes insert a new row with EFFECTIVE_FROM; the old row gets EFFECTIVE_TO. Any query that forgets the date predicate picks up 2019 slabs. SP_CalculateTax joins on @InvoiceDate BETWEEN EFFECTIVE_FROM AND ISNULL(EFFECTIVE_TO, "9999-12-31").
memory.reason: Historical invoices must reprint with the rate that was live on their date.

memory.title: TRANS_INVOICE has no FK to MST_CUSTOMER — it is enforced in code only
memory.body: The FK was dropped in 2016 during a bulk-import project and never restored. 1,148 stored procs assume it is absent. Adding it back fails on 4,207 orphan rows from the 2014 migration.
memory.reason: Legacy data quality; restoring the constraint is a project, not a task.

memory.title: Never add a non-filtered index to TRANS_INVOICE during business hours
memory.body: The table is 41 GB / 96 M rows. An online index build still pushed CPU to 94 % and the invoice screen timed out for 8 minutes on 2025-11-30. Index work is a 01:00–03:30 IST window only, with SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON.
memory.reason: Production incident #52.

memory.title: PMI patient identity is (HOSP_CODE, MR_NO) — MR_NO alone is not unique
memory.body: Three hospitals share the schema and each restarted MR numbering in 2019. Any join on MR_NO without HOSP_CODE mixes patients across sites.
memory.reason: Discovered during the OPD dedup task; 1,900 false merges were prevented.

memory.title: SP_CalculateTax is called from 23 places, 6 of them outside the invoice module
memory.body: Callers include SP_PostTransaction, SP_CreateCreditNote, the Crystal report RPT_TaxSummary, the nightly SSIS package PKG_TaxRecon, and two Excel-linked views used by finance. Any signature change is a 23-point blast radius.
memory.reason: Impact analysis for TASK-492 — a parameter add was rejected because of this.

memory.title: The 2011 VB6 tax module is still the source of truth for rounding parity
memory.body: legacy/TaxCalc.bas was ported line-by-line into TaxService.cs in 2018. Where the C# looks wrong, check the .bas first — the "bug" is usually intentional parity with 11 years of posted data.
memory.reason: Two rewrites were reverted for breaking historical reprints.

memory.title: Module 17 (Excise) is dead code but cannot be deleted
memory.body: Excise was replaced by GST in 2017. The screens are hidden but SP_PostTransaction still writes TRANS_EXCISE rows with zeros because a statutory archive job reads them until FY2029.
memory.reason: Statutory retention.

memory.title: Crystal Reports still renders 61 of 88 ERP reports
memory.body: Report changes need the CR runtime on the build agent and a .rpt round-trip through the Windows designer. Agents cannot edit .rpt files — they open a task for the human with the exact field list.
memory.reason: Binary format, no CI story.

memory.title: Session state lives in IIS in-process memory across 3 nodes with no affinity
memory.body: The load balancer round-robins without sticky sessions, so a user whose next request lands on another node loses their session. This is the root cause behind TASK-501, not the 20-minute timeout everyone assumed.
memory.reason: Never migrated to SQL session state after the 2019 scale-out.

memory.title: BUG-883 — CGST/SGST reversed on interstate orders after branch transfer
memory.body: TaxService.ResolveJurisdiction compared MST_CUSTOMER.STATE_CODE against the *login* branch instead of the invoice branch. After the Pune branch transfer in August, 41 invoices split as CGST/SGST when they should have been IGST. Fix is one line plus a backfill migration.
memory.reason: Wrong comparison operand; the login branch is only correct when the user never switches branch.

memory.title: Bulk upload times out above ~28k rows on the shared staging server
memory.body: The chunked endpoint holds one transaction per chunk; at 28k rows tempdb spills and the request exceeds the 120 s IIS limit. Chunk size 2,000 with a per-chunk commit clears it.
memory.reason: tempdb on staging is 8 GB versus 96 GB in production, so the ceiling only shows up in QA.

memory.title: Date pickers send local time; the API assumes UTC — off-by-one on invoices posted after 18:30 IST
memory.body: The React date picker serialises with toISOString(), shifting IST dates back a day after 18:30. Fixed in 6 screens, still open in RPT filters and the ageing report.
memory.reason: No shared date serialisation helper existed until 2026-04.

memory.title: HIMS OPD queue duplicates a token when the print job fails
memory.body: The token number increments before the print acknowledgement, so a paper jam creates a gap and the retry issues a second live token for the same patient. Reception works around it manually at 3 sites.
memory.reason: Print acknowledgement is fire-and-forget.

memory.title: ADR-52 — every transaction write goes through SP_PostTransaction
memory.body: Accepted 2024-11-06, superseding the 2019 "direct write with audit trigger" approach. The trigger version double-counted on multi-row inserts. Status: accepted, no supersession pending.
memory.reason: Auditability and a single place to stamp the ledger.

memory.title: Production incident #38 — ledger drift of ₹18.4 L across 2,106 invoices
memory.body: A 2024 data-fix script updated TRANS_INVOICE.NET_AMOUNT directly to correct a discount error. TRANS_LEDGER was never touched, so the trial balance drifted for 6 weeks before month-end caught it. Recovery took 9 days of manual reconciliation with the auditors.
memory.reason: Direct TRANS write bypassed SP_PostTransaction.

memory.title: Production incident #47 — deploy at 17:40 IST collided with the GST return window
memory.body: A backend deploy recycled the app pool while 60+ users were filing GSTR-1. Deploys are now blocked between 09:00 and 20:00 IST on the 1st–11th of each month, enforced in the pipeline, not by memory.
memory.reason: Statutory filing window.

memory.title: Production incident #52 — index build spiked CPU to 94 % for 8 minutes
memory.body: An "online" index build on TRANS_INVOICE during business hours starved the invoice screen. Trigger for the 01:00–03:30 maintenance window rule.
memory.reason: 41 GB table on a shared instance; ONLINE = ON is not free.

memory.title: InvoiceService.cs is 2,914 lines and owns 7 responsibilities
memory.body: Tax, discount, dispatch note, e-way bill, credit note, print and export all live in one class. The team decided against splitting it during TASK-492 — the split is its own epic with its own regression budget.
memory.reason: PM rule: no unrequested refactor inside a bug-fix task.

memory.title: C# naming here is class-object style: InvoiceService invoiceService = new()
memory.body: Variables mirror the type name in camelCase. Not _svc, not svc, not invSvc. The reviewer agent flags abbreviations as a style rejection.
memory.reason: PM standard applied across all C# in every project.

memory.title: Tests live beside the module: tests/<Module>/<Class>Tests.cs, xUnit + FluentAssertions
memory.body: No NUnit, no MSTest, no Moq — the codebase uses hand-written fakes because Moq broke on the 2022 sealed-class sweep. Test method names read Should_Split_IGST_When_Interstate.
memory.reason: Consistency with 3,100 existing tests.

memory.title: ERP renewal is module-by-module; 12 of 47 modules are on the new stack
memory.body: Old and new run side by side behind the same IIS site. A module is "done" only when its Crystal reports are ported or explicitly deferred. Billing is the current module; inventory is next.
memory.reason: Big-bang rewrite was rejected in 2023 after the HIMS v2 attempt.

memory.title: Release train is Tuesday 21:30 IST; hotfixes need a named approver
memory.body: Anything merged after Monday 18:00 waits for the next train. Hotfix path exists but requires the human PM to approve in the Approvals queue with a one-line justification.
memory.reason: Support staff are only available Tue/Wed morning for fallout.

memory.title: Show the plan before touching a file — every time, no exceptions
memory.body: Agents post a numbered plan with file paths and expected diff size, wait for the approve click, then run. Even for a one-line fix. The PM reads plans faster than diffs.
memory.reason: Explicit standing instruction; violated twice in June and both runs were reverted.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2026-06-03 ("show the plan first, then touch the code")

memory.title: Terminal-dense UI, no marketing dashboards
memory.body: Small type, tight rows, flat surfaces, one accent colour. Gradients, glass, big shadows and hero cards get rejected on sight. Numbers are tabular; IDs and paths are monospace.
memory.reason: The PM lives in this UI 9 hours a day and wants density over decoration.

memory.title: Cost ceiling: ₹4,000/day across all agents; local models first
memory.body: Qwen3-Coder-Next and Qwen3-Next-80B run on the local box at zero marginal cost. Paid models are for reasoning and review only. Crossing 80 % of the ceiling pauses autonomous agents.
memory.reason: Single-operator business, no funding.

memory.title: The PM writes requirements informally — never ask for them to be rewritten as a formal spec
memory.body: "Invoice tax is wrong: the CGST/SGST split comes out reversed on interstate orders. Fix it." That is a complete requirement. The Commander compiles it; the PM does not expand it. Asking for a formal spec is treated as friction.
memory.reason: He types fast and informally; forcing a formal spec costs him time and loses nuance.

memory.title: Strict SOLID — he will reject working code that violates it
memory.body: Single responsibility and interface-first are non-negotiable for new C#. He has sent back a passing PR because a service did two things. Existing violations stay until their own task; new ones never ship.
memory.reason: 14 years of maintaining a codebase where nobody enforced it.
memory.source: Review history: 23 rejections citing SRP or DIP

memory.title: He hates unrequested refactors — fix the bug, nothing else
memory.body: A diff that also renames variables, reorders methods or "cleans up" nearby code gets reverted whole, even when the fix inside it is correct. If a refactor is needed, open a separate task and let him schedule it.
memory.reason: Review time is his bottleneck; a 400-line diff for a 3-line fix is unreviewable.
memory.source: PM instruction repeated 7 times + 4 full reverts

memory.title: Prefers the existing pattern over a better one
memory.body: If the codebase already does X in an ugly way in 40 places, the 41st does it the same way. "Consistency beats correctness" is a direct quote. New patterns need an ADR and his sign-off first.
memory.reason: He is the only maintainer; two patterns means twice the context to hold.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2025-04-22 ("use the pattern that is already there")

memory.title: Tests must actually be run — "tests likhe hain" is not enough
memory.body: Every handoff needs pasted runner output: the command, pass/fail counts and the duration. Claiming coverage without a run is the fastest way to lose his trust; he has caught it three times.
memory.reason: Two agents in 2025 reported green on tests that never executed.

memory.title: Works 10:30–02:00 IST; approvals stall between 03:00 and 10:00
memory.body: Queue HIGH-risk gates before 01:00 or they sit until late morning. He answers Telegram faster than the in-app queue between 22:00 and 01:00.
memory.reason: Observed across 6 months of approval timestamps.

memory.title: Reads the diff, not the summary — keep PR bodies short and file lists exact
memory.body: Three lines of why, then the file list. Long agent-written PR descriptions get skimmed and the actual review happens in the diff view. Never bury a schema change in prose.
memory.reason: Stated preference, confirmed by review-time telemetry (median 9 s on the body, 4 min in the diff).

conflicts.detail: MEM-324 says session state is IIS in-process across 3 nodes with no affinity. The DevOps runbook fact behind MEM-808 claims sticky sessions were enabled at the load balancer in 2025-10. Both cannot be true — TASK-501 depends on which one is.
conflicts.suggestion: Ask DevOps agent to read the live F5 pool config, then retire the loser.
